transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-20 09:30 UTC
Duration: 1:25
Attendees: Jordan, Sofia, Ethan, Priya, Ava, Liam, Maya, Noah, Zara
---
Auto-summary (auto-gen): internal dry-run to validate deprioritize policy and fallback routing before launch window.
---
[00:00:05] Jordan Kim: okay, let's get started, I think we have about an hour twenty five, thank you everyone for making time, quick agenda: run through the deprioritization rules, the dry-run steps, and then a shorter war room of the canary plan.
[00:00:28] Ava Patel: quick note — product wants this to be low-risk, so anything that might block embeddings or long-poll jobs we need a skip.
[00:00:40] Sofia Martinez: noted, we'll keep heavy requests on Dedicated and make sure hosted falls back to smaller chunk models, um, but we should enumerate what "smaller" means.
[00:00:55] Ethan Cho: timeline check — we're slotted to flip traffic next Friday, so ideally the staging dry-run happens tomorrow or Thursday.
[00:01:08] Priya Nair: staging is ready for synthetic but we need the canary throttle knob prepared, right now it's a manual switch in the orchestrator.
[00:01:22] Noah Brooks: manual switches are ok for dry-run but we should exercise the automated policy path, like the circuit-breaker that lowers batch size and routes to quantized model variant.
[00:01:38] Maya Singh: also, don't forget RBAC for the runbook updates — support needs read-only and ops needs execute.
[00:01:52] Zara Hsu: I'll take RBAC in the runbook, also add a QA checklist item for prefix/KV cache clearer, sometimes K-V cash persists weirdly in staging and we get false positives. (laughs)
[00:02:05] Jordan Kim: (laughs) K-V cash, that's a new one. Ok, first substantive item: deprioritization criteria. Sofia?
[00:02:18] Sofia Martinez: right, we proposed three tiers: soft deprioritize for non-critical routes — e.g. bulk embeddings, long async tasks; medium deprioritize for interactive batch ops where latency above 500ms is acceptable; hard deprioritize for any request hitting per-tenant quota anomalies. The policy maps to routing changes: reduce batch size, switch to quantized model variant, or route to Dedicated pool depending on account tier.
[00:02:52] Liam O'Connor: question — how do we detect per-tenant quota anomalies without spamming alerts? We need a windowed anomaly detector, otherwise every spike triggers a deprio.
[00:03:06] Priya Nair: we have a sliding window on QPS and token-rate, currently set to 30s window with 3x baseline threshold. For this launch we proposed a slightly wider 45s window to avoid flapping.
[00:03:20] Ava Patel: wider windows sound fine, but doc how that impacts SLOs, we need to present to customer success.
[00:03:33] Jordan Kim: noted. Next — fallback routing. Sofia, can you sketch the route map?
[00:03:41] Sofia Martinez: yes, so primary path: Hosted api -> model v2-xx (full FP) for interactive. On deprio: path A is quantized v2-q for same host region; path B is route to Dedicated pool (if customer committed) with burst tags; path C is regional fallback to eu-west or us-central depending on latency budget. We also have forced-accept where we drop to short-answer mode for very long context.
[00:04:09] Maya Singh: how do we communicate a short-answer mode to end-users? We need structured error/metadata so clients can opt to re-try differently.
[00:04:20] Sofia Martinez: yeah, we'll add a structured header: x-redwood-degrade: short_answer|quantized|dedicated_fallback. Clients can read and render a notice.
[00:04:33] Noah Brooks: slight nit — some clients will break on unfamiliar headers, should be safe as optional.
[00:04:40] Ethan Cho: telemetry — what are the essential metrics we need in the dry-run?
[00:04:46] Priya Nair: P50/P95/P99 latencies, token cost per request, route switch counts, cache hit ratio, and number of degraded responses returned. Also we need a simple quality proxy: top-level hallucination detect is hard, but we can measure completion length dropoff and token reuse rates as a proxy.
[00:05:07] Zara Hsu: QA can add a small prompt set to measure regressions; not perfect but it'll catch major breakages.
[00:05:15] Jordan Kim: good. Now let's walk the dry-run script. Sofia, run us through the steps and estimated times.
[00:05:23] Sofia Martinez: step 1 — baseline load: 10 minutes at normal QPS. step 2 — inject a sustained surge: 20 minutes increasing token-rate to 3x. step 3 — flip deprioritization soft then medium then hard, each for 10 minutes. step 4 — simulate tenant quota spike and force per-owner routing. step 5 — rollback sequence and verify telemetry. Whole script ~60 minutes plus buffer.
[00:05:52] Liam O'Connor: do we run this against a staging model catalog identical to prod? Because quantization can change behavior.
[00:05:59] Sofia Martinez: yes, staging has v2-xx and v2-q builds but note that the q build in staging is on different kernel set so perf numbers will differ slightly.
[00:06:12] Priya Nair: also, KV cache eviction test — when we evict prefix cache, we sometimes see longer latencies for the first request, we need to capture that micro spike.
[00:06:23] Zara Hsu: I'll add explicit cache-evict TTLs and a warm-up period.
[00:06:30] Jordan Kim: great. Now canary throttle knob — Sofia?
[00:06:35] Sofia Martinez: current knob is a rate-limiter that decreases batch size and enforces a min token cap; for canary we'll enable an automated policy that triggers at 3 degradations/min for the route and drops batch size by 30%. If after 5 minutes there's no improvement, route traffic to region fallback.
[00:06:54] Maya Singh: timelines for automation — how quickly can we flip it from manual to auto?
[00:06:59] Priya Nair: we can enable auto in staging today; prod needs a quick feature flag path and a guardrail — manual approval override.
[00:07:09] Noah Brooks: I want a safety escape hatch: a single button to freeze model-rollout and pin to last-known-good variant.
[00:07:16] Ethan Cho: agreed, we'll add that to Console as "freeze rollout" and log the actor.
[00:07:23] Ava Patel: and audit log must be shipper to the event stream for postmortem.
[00:07:29] Jordan Kim: excellent. Let's pause for clarifying questions.
[00:07:36] (silence)
[00:07:40] Liam O'Connor: minor — do we have a mapping of customer tiers to Dedicated pools? Some enterprise accounts will expect no routing to public hosted.
[00:07:51] Sofia Martinez: yes, enterprise flag prevents hosted fallback; for those we only allow route to org-dedicated or fail closed as an option.
[00:08:03] Maya Singh: that implies we need consent screen and pre-notify for those customers before any deprioritization policy takes effect.
[00:08:12] Jordan Kim: make that a checkbox in the rollout config.
[00:08:17] Zara Hsu: QA question — do we have synthetic clients that will respect the x-redwood-degrade header?
[00:08:25] Priya Nair: yes, our synthetic harness will record and surface header counts.
[00:08:30] Sofia Martinez: ok, moving to failure scenarios — Sofia reading worst-case: if Dedicated pool runs OOM on quantized variant, we need fallback to another region with degraded outputs; but we also need to avoid double routing loops.
[00:08:50] Noah Brooks: double routing loops are a risk; include a route-hop counter in the request metadata to prevent infinite retries.
[00:08:58] Ethan Cho: good call.
[00:09:02] Jordan Kim: communications plan — who notifies customers if we perform an aggressive deprioritization?
[00:09:08] Maya Singh: CS will get a pre-notify if the threshold is expected; otherwise post-incident summary. For premium customers we will ping the account directly.
[00:09:17] Ava Patel: also notify the growth slack channel so product can see any UX impact.
[00:09:22] Jordan Kim: final area — rollback criteria and metrics for success. Priya?
[00:09:27] Priya Nair: success metrics: P95 < 750ms after downgrade, overall error rate < 0.5%, degradation header count less than 10% of traffic, and no sustained increase in hallucination proxy. If not met, rollback.
[00:09:45] Liam O'Connor: can we codify that into an automated monitor?
[00:09:49] Priya Nair: yes, deck monitors can flip slack alerts and page SRE.
[00:09:55] Jordan Kim: ok let's run the actual dry-run sequencing questions — who runs step execution?
[00:09:59] Maya Singh: I'll lead the execution, Priya and Zara will watch telemetry, Noah will be on route-mapping, Ethan will sign off. Jordan will coordinate comms.
[00:10:10] Jordan Kim: perfect. Quick pause — any outstanding legal/compliance items?
[00:10:14] Ethan Cho: none for this deprioritization activity, data stays in staging. For customers that require data residency we need to ensure regional fallbacks respect that; we do have controls in the routing policy.
[00:10:26] Jordan Kim: good. OK jumping ahead — live walk: Sofia will simulate a medium deprio and Priya will show telemetry.
[00:10:33] Sofia Martinez: starting now, initiating medium deprio on /v1/chat.
[00:10:38] [00:10:38] Priya Nair: telemetry spike: P99 up 1.4x then drops as batch size reduced, route-switch count +17. Cache hit rate dips 6%.
[00:10:49] Zara Hsu: QA note — observed a few truncated completions on long-context prompts, marking as failure if >5% of long-context tests fail.
[00:10:59] Noah Brooks: route-hop counter looks okay, no loops.
[00:11:05] Jordan Kim: good. Stop test and review.
[00:11:09] Sofia Martinez: stopping. Lessons learned: eviction spike visible, need a brief warm-up step after cache clear, and the quantized responses shortened answers — acceptable for chat but not for some product flows.
[00:11:25] Ava Patel: product: make a list of flows that cannot accept shortened answers.
[00:11:30] Ethan Cho: I'll own that list and annotate rollout.
[00:11:33] Jordan Kim: time check — we're at ~41 minutes in, we have more to cover: canary knob thresholds and runbook publishing.
[00:11:41] Sofia Martinez: canary knob: default trigger at 3 degradations/min, drop batch size by 30%, after 5 minutes escalate to region fallback. We also set an upper bound on quantized model usage per minute so we don't exceed token budget.
[00:11:59] Priya Nair: one more note — quantized model has different memory profile; in staging we saw occasional kernel fallback on old GPUs, need to add kernel-fallback logging to the telemetry for the dry-run.
[00:12:12] Zara Hsu: I'll include kernel fallback checks in QA.
[00:12:17] Maya Singh: publishing runbook — we need a short checklist at the top for the oncall person and a longer playbook below. Also a cutover note for the launch window.
[00:12:29] Noah Brooks: include a "who to call" list with escalation matrix.
[00:12:33] Jordan Kim: agreed. Wrap-up: three immediate things — QA checklist update, publish emergency route map, canary throttle config. Who's doing what?
[00:12:44] Zara Hsu: QA checklist update, due 10/25.
[00:12:47] Priya Nair: emergency route map and console runbook update, due 10/22.
[00:12:50] Sofia Martinez: canary config and knob parameters, due 10/23.
[00:12:54] Ethan Cho: I'll circulate a short pre-notify template for CS.
[00:12:58] Jordan Kim: cool. Any last minute questions?
[00:13:02] (background chatter)
[00:13:08] Ava Patel: do we want a second dry-run with real-ish customer personas?
[00:13:12] Maya Singh: yes, let's do a follow-up next week with two personas, enterprise and freemium.
[00:13:19] Jordan Kim: excellent. Alright meeting adjourned.
---
